content.text: The PUT endpoint is a full replacement, so I'll GET the dashboard, append a new panel built from the existing bar-chart panel's structure, and PUT the full object back. The new panel is a count of requests terms-bucketed on `host.keyword`, placed in a new row below the existing two.

input.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/claude-0/-tmp-eff-3uk11yem-work/0da1e72d-e9d9-58d9-b388-fca8d0eba393/scratchpad && cd $_ 2>/dev/null; cat > add_host_panel.py <<'EOF'
import copy, json, os, sys, urllib.request

base = os.environ["KIBANA_URL"]
key = os.environ["KIBANA_TEST_API_KEY"]
dash_id = "study-seed-site-health"
url = f"{base}/api/dashboards/{dash_id}"
hdrs = {"kbn-xsrf": "true", "Authorization": f"ApiKey {key}", "Content-Type": "application/json"}

def call(method, body=None):
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, method=method, headers=hdrs,
                                 data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None)
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as r:
        return json.load(r)

current = call("GET")
data = current["data"]
print("panels before:", len(data["panels"]))

# Mirror the existing bar chart (response code) and change it to terms on host.keyword, count
template = next(p for p in data["panels"] if p["config"]["title"] == "Requests by response code")
new_panel = copy.deepcopy(template)
new_panel["grid"] = {"x": 0, "y": 12, "w": 24, "h": 12}
new_panel["config"]["title"] = "Requests by host"
layer = new_panel["config"]["layers"][0]
layer["x"]["fields"] = ["host.keyword"]
data["panels"].append(new_panel)

result = call("PUT", data)
print("PUT ok; panels after:", len(data["panels"]))
print(json.dumps(result)[:300])
EOF
python3 add_host_panel.py
